Preconditions: Docker Compose deployed on network host
ReproducibleSteps: Inspect docker-compose.yml Redis port exposure and authentication command
ExpectedBehavior: Redis requires password/ACL and binds strictly to internal container network without unauthenticated host exposure
ObservedBehavior: Redis published on host port 6380 without requirepass or ACL configured
Evidence: git grep "6380:6379" docker-compose.yml; lack of requirepass in redis command
RootCause: Compose file published port for dev convenience without requiring authentication
Impact: Remote host attacker can connect to Redis, read cached customer PII, poison session tokens, or tamper with BullMQ queues
ProposedRemediation: Remove host port mapping or require strong password/ACL in command and env config

Preconditions: Attempt to run release certification check
ExpectedBehavior: Certification passes only when all gates are green and git SHA matches certified commit
ObservedBehavior: Command exits 1: Certificate status is WITHDRAWN, schema hash mismatch, commit mismatch
Evidence: Exit Code 1 from verify-certification-validity.js; stdout reports WITHDRAWN
RootCause: Certificate was invalidated due to unverified staging/operational gates and schema mutation
Impact: Application cannot be certified or promoted to production without authorized sign-off
ProposedRemediation: Complete Phase C/D gates, perform real staging migration, and re-sign certificate with new schema hash

Preconditions: Claim exists in SETTLED or CLOSED state
ExpectedBehavior: Endpoint rejects request with 400 Bad Request or 409 Conflict because claim is in terminal state
ObservedBehavior: Endpoint directly updates approvedAmount on settled/closed claim without state machine check
Evidence: Controller calls prisma.claim.update directly; ClaimStateMachine is not invoked
RootCause: Financial records and general ledger disagree with claim approved amount; fraud/tampering risk
Impact: Route claim updates through domain command verifying state is non-terminal and emit audit event

ReproducibleSteps: Send POST /webhooks/unknown-provider with forged event payload
ExpectedBehavior: Controller rejects unconfigured/unknown providers with 401 Unauthorized
ObservedBehavior: validateSignature only checks razorpay; other providers fall through and emit unauthenticated events
Evidence: Source code: validateSignature only contains if (provider === "razorpay") block
RootCause: Missing default-deny branch in webhook signature validation logic
Impact: Unauthenticated attacker can inject arbitrary provider events into internal outbox/event bus
ProposedRemediation: Allow-list known providers, require signature verification for every provider, reject unknown with 401

Preconditions: Back Office user views finance page
ExpectedBehavior: System calls backend API POST /finance/receipts, creates persistent receipt, and displays real receipt number
ObservedBehavior: Button displays toast.success("Receipt REC-2026-9901 issued successfully") with zero API calls or DB writes
Evidence: Source code in page.tsx shows hardcoded toast with REC-2026-9901 and no network request
RootCause: Placeholder mock UI action was never wired to backend receipt service
Impact: Operators believe financial receipt was issued and provided to customer when no document exists
ProposedRemediation: Wire button to real receipts mutation hook or disable button until backend command is ready

ObservedBehavior: Component only triggers toast.success("Download started") without any network request or file transfer

ObservedBehavior: Button triggers an informational toast on a completely read-only view; changes are lost on refresh

Preconditions: Agent records customer notes or dismisses alerts
ReproducibleSteps: Enter customer note on one browser, open same customer on second browser/device
ExpectedBehavior: Customer notes and task state are persisted in CRM database and visible across all authorized agents
ObservedBehavior: Notes and dismissed alerts are saved to localStorage under browser-local key; invisible to other agents
RootCause: Frontend state used localStorage instead of backend CustomerNotes API
Impact: Critical underwriting notes and customer history lost across devices or on browser cache clear
ProposedRemediation: Persist customer notes to backend CustomerNotes table with companyId scope and audit trail

Preconditions: Calculate OD premium for vehicle with high IDV
ReproducibleSteps: Calculate OD premium for IDV 3,000,000, Zone A (rate 0.03127), multiplier 1.15
ExpectedBehavior: Calculated premium should match exact decimal half-up rounding (107,882 INR)
ObservedBehavior: Binary floating point yields 107881.49999999999 which rounds down to 107,881 INR (1 rupee error)
Evidence: Reproducible arithmetic check: 3000000 * 0.03127 * 1.15 in JS yields 107881.49999999999
RootCause: Use of raw JavaScript number floating-point multiplication instead of exact decimal arithmetic
Impact: Quotation total differs by 1 rupee from statutory insurer tariff; reconciliation discrepancies
ProposedRemediation: Adopt exact decimal arithmetic (e.g. decimal.js or integer paise arithmetic) throughout calculation engine

Preconditions: Run deep system churn benchmark against PostgreSQL
ExpectedBehavior: All 10 core entities pass persistence and required column integrity assertions
ObservedBehavior: MotorInspection check fails: missing required photo keys or inspectionCode; Policy history audit check fails
Evidence: Report output from deep-system-churn-report.json Section 8: unexpectedFailures: 2
RootCause: Inspection creation does not enforce all 7 photographic keys before approval state transition
Impact: Non-compliant vehicle inspections can be approved without mandatory statutory evidence
ProposedRemediation: Enforce validation requiring all 7 image keys in MotorInspectionService.approveInspection

ReproducibleSteps: Migration runs in dry-run mode by default and wraps all database writes in an atomic transaction
ExpectedBehavior: CLI defaults to write run (dryRun: false), and mutations are executed outside a Prisma transaction
ObservedBehavior: Source code inspection of motor-migration-01.ts and motor-migration.service.ts
Evidence: No $transaction wrapper around multi-step deduplication and case re-linking
RootCause: A network failure or partial crash leaves database in corrupt, partially-migrated state with detached policies
Impact: Default to dry-run mode, require explicit --apply, and wrap all operations in a single interactive transaction

Preconditions: Compare Node.js versions in ci.yml vs deploy.yml vs production-remediation-ci.yml
ReproducibleSteps: All workflows use identical, pinned Node.js runtime version matching production image
ExpectedBehavior: ci.yml pins Node 20; deploy.yml pins Node 24; production-remediation-ci.yml pins Node 24
ObservedBehavior: Workflow YAML inspections: node-version: 20 vs node-version: 24
Evidence: Uncoordinated updates across multiple workflow files without central .nvmrc reference
RootCause: Code compiled and tested on Node 20 may encounter runtime regressions or native module errors on Node 24
Impact: Pin single supported Node.js version (e.g. Node 22 LTS or 20 LTS) via .nvmrc across all workflows and Dockerfiles

FileAndLine: Run test suite in CI workflow
ReproducibleSteps: Jest interprets --runInBand as an option and executes tests sequentially
ExpectedBehavior: Extra "--" separator causes Jest to treat --runInBand as a filename pattern, resulting in 0 tests executed
ObservedBehavior: Local reproduction: pnpm --filter api test:cert -- --runInBand exited 1 with "Pattern --runInBand, 0 tests run"
Evidence: Incorrect argument passing syntax for pnpm command forwarding to Jest
RootCause: CI workflow fails or silently skips test execution
Impact: Remove extra "--" separator in workflow YAML invocation

FileAndLine: Run test:cert on Windows development machine
ReproducibleSteps: Test runner executes all certification suites without memory exhaustion
ExpectedBehavior: Jest parallel workers run out of memory (JavaScript heap out of memory / ENOMEM) and crash
ObservedBehavior: Process output: FATAL ERROR: MarkCompactCollector: young object promotion failed Allocation failed
Evidence: Default Jest parallel worker configuration spawns multiple NestJS compile contexts simultaneously
RootCause: Developers cannot reliably run test:cert without adding --runInBand or increasing Node heap size
Impact: Add --runInBand or configure maxWorkers: 2 and NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=4096" in test:cert script

ReproducibleSteps: Repository query includes companyId in where clause before fetching relational records
ExpectedBehavior: Repository query fetches claim and hydrates all related PII (policy, contact, account) using ID only, before service-level authorization
ObservedBehavior: Source code: findById({ where: { id, deletedAt: null }, include: { ... } })
Evidence: Tenancy filter deferred to ResourceAuthorizationService instead of repository query predicate
RootCause: Cross-tenant record data materialized in application memory unnecessarily; potential timing oracle
Impact: Add companyId parameter to claimRepository.findById and enforce in database query predicate
